"In a shocking revelation, it has been discovered that Northern Territory police failed to act on multiple self-harm and suicide attempts in caged police vehicles, ultimately leading to the death of a 23-year-old man," reported the Guardian.

Coroner Greg Cavanagh criticized the police for not heeding an internal recommendation to install CCTV cameras in caged vehicles back in 2013, after a previous death in custody. In the three years following this recommendation, there were at least 16 attempted suicides in these vehicles, with some individuals being found semi-conscious or unconscious before being detected.

Cavanagh's findings revealed a disturbing trend of neglect and inaction within the NT police force, stating that it was only a matter of time before a tragedy occurred. This tragedy struck on 16 September last year, when officers stumbled upon a serious crash involving a Toyota Hilux and a palm tree.

Dale Scott Walkinshaw, the 23-year-old driver, was found holding his injured passenger in his arms. The young woman, who had been with Walkinshaw at a bar earlier that night, was in critical condition. Walkinshaw himself was over the legal limit, indicating that he had been driving under the influence.

This heartbreaking incident serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of police negligence and the urgent need for reform within the Northern Territory law enforcement. The failure to act on previous warnings and recommendations has resulted in a tragic loss of life that could have been prevented.
